acceptance_test_matrix: DROP_NEW sustained overrun: newest arrivals are rejected while previously queued entries remain ordered and drain correctly.
DROP_OLD sustained overrun: oldest queued entries are evicted, newer accepted entries drain correctly, and capacity invariants hold.
BLOCK sustained overrun: producer admission blocks or waits without data loss, resumes after drain, and does not propagate across partitions.
OVERFLOW_TO_DISK sustained overrun: excess entries spill through MmapJournal and drain in the expected order.
Overflow spill readback: spill file contents are read back during drain and no duplicate or missing entries occur.
Edge-level hot-swap: changing one edge policy affects only that edge and takes effect for subsequent enqueue decisions.
R-002 prerequisite coverage: existing snapshot/journal lifecycle assumptions are detected before implementation and remain compatible after overflow spill integration.

Lifecycle failure coverage: stale or invalid spill files, invariant or CRC-equivalent failure, spill append failure, partial drain failure, and cleanup paths fail closed without partial acceptance or broken lifecycle invariants.
Configured QA gates: qa/smoke.sh, qa/regression.sh, jmhSmokeCheck, and allocation gate remain green.
assumptions: GraphPartitionRunner owns runtime edge queues and is the correct boundary for policy enforcement and hot-swap.
BackpressurePolicy is a fixed public API enum, not a custom extension point or callback mechanism.
dag-framework-api owns public policy symbols and builder-facing configuration while runtime-core owns runtime edge behavior.
dag-framework-lvc contains reusable MmapJournal machinery from the lvc-standard path and must be reused for overflow spill persistence.

R-006 is dependency-gated on the existing R-002 snapshot/journal lifecycle contract; design and implementation must first confirm the prerequisite is present and compatible, then integrate without redefining snapshot semantics.
Policy hot-swap is edge-scoped, visible to concurrent producers and consumers, and must not propagate backpressure across partitions.
Existing qa/smoke.sh, qa/regression.sh, jmhSmokeCheck, and allocation gates are authoritative verification gates for this feature.

acceptance_tests: DROP_NEW sustained overrun rejects newest arrivals while previously queued entries remain ordered and drain correctly.
DROP_OLD sustained overrun evicts oldest queued entries, admits newer entries, and preserves capacity invariants.
BLOCK sustained overrun blocks producer admission until capacity is available, does not lose data, and does not propagate cross-partition backpressure.
OVERFLOW_TO_DISK sustained overrun spills excess entries through MmapJournal and drains them in deterministic order.
Overflow spill readback verifies persisted payloads and proves no duplicate or missing entries across in-memory and mmap-backed boundaries.
Edge-level hot-swap changes behavior only for the configured edge and applies to subsequent enqueue decisions without corrupting existing buffered or spilled records.
R-002 snapshot/journal prerequisite compatibility is explicitly checked before implementation and remains intact after R-006 changes.
Stale or invalid spill files are rejected or recovered according to existing journal invariants.
Invariant or CRC-equivalent MmapJournal validation failures fail closed without silent data corruption or partial acceptance.
Spill append, drain interruption, and partial failure paths leave queue, spill, and runner lifecycle invariants intact.
qa/smoke.sh, qa/regression.sh, jmhSmokeCheck, and allocation gates pass.
design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Each edge reads its current BackpressurePolicy atomically at enqueue time. Hot-swap updates must be thread-safe and edge-local. BLOCK may block only the producing path for the configured overrun edge. DROP_NEW and DROP_OLD must preserve deterministic queue capacity and ordering invariants under concurrent producers and consumers. OVERFLOW_TO_DISK must serialize spill append and drain so in-memory and spilled entries are observed exactly once in documented edge order.
forbidden_alternatives: Stringly typed policy selectors.
User-supplied policy callbacks.
Priority queues or priority-aware drop rules.
Global runtime backpressure state shared across partitions.
Blocking all partitions or upstream graph execution for one overrun edge.
A new spill encoder or non-MmapJournal overflow format.
Snapshot or journal lifecycle reimplementation outside the existing R-002-compatible machinery.
Test-only behavior switches that bypass production policy implementation.
hard_constraints: Do not add custom backpressure policies or public extension hooks.
Do not add priority-based shedding or conflation.
Do not add cross-partition backpressure propagation.
Do not rebuild the graph runner to implement policy hot-swap.
Do not invent a bespoke spill file format outside MmapJournal.
Do not redefine, bypass, or reimplement the R-002 snapshot/journal lifecycle prerequisite inside R-006.
Allocation gate must stay green.
jmhSmokeCheck must remain green.
qa/smoke.sh and qa/regression.sh must pass.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: dag-framework-api defines the stable public enum and builder/configuration surface; runtime-core implements edge queue admission, DROP_NEW, DROP_OLD, BLOCK, policy dispatch, hot-swap state, and sustained-overrun behavior; dag-framework-lvc provides MmapJournal primitives reused for overflow spill persistence; QA roots contain only tests and fixtures.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: OVERFLOW_TO_DISK must reuse MmapJournal machinery from dag-framework-lvc/lvc-standard, preserve edge record order across in-memory and spilled entries, read back spilled payloads during drain, clean up or close spill resources after normal drain and failure cleanup, reject stale or invalid spill state, fail closed on invariant or CRC-equivalent validation failure without duplicate delivery, silent loss, or partial acceptance, and remain compatible with the existing R-002 snapshot/journal lifecycle contract.
design_contract.public_api: Add public enum BackpressurePolicy with exactly DROP_NEW, DROP_OLD, BLOCK, and OVERFLOW_TO_DISK; expose default and per-edge policy configuration through GraphPartitionRunner.Builder keyed by edge identity; expose edge-level policy hot-swap through a runtime-scoped method or handle without custom policy callbacks.

final.problem_statement: Implement the R-006 backpressure policy selector so GraphPartitionRunner.Builder exposes per-edge DROP_NEW, DROP_OLD, BLOCK, and OVERFLOW_TO_DISK behavior under sustained overrun, including mmap-backed overflow spill, deterministic drain/readback, edge-level policy hot-swap, and prerequisite-safe integration with the existing snapshot/journal lifecycle.
risk_register: BackpressurePolicy API placement could leak runtime-only concerns into dag-framework-api or conflict with existing builder compatibility expectations.
R-006 may be implemented before confirming the R-002 snapshot/journal prerequisite, causing incompatible spill lifecycle behavior.
BLOCK behavior may deadlock or stall unrelated edges if enqueue and drain paths share executor or lock ownership incorrectly.
DROP_NEW and DROP_OLD can produce off-by-one capacity behavior under sustained overrun if edge buffer boundaries are unclear.
DROP_OLD could violate ordering or cleanup/release guarantees if eviction races with drain.
Policy hot-swap can race with active producers or drainers and mix semantics for a single accepted record unless policy references are atomic and edge-local.
OVERFLOW_TO_DISK may reorder records between memory and disk if append/drain boundaries are not serialized.
MmapJournal reuse may accidentally bypass existing invariant checks, cleanup lifecycle, or validation failure handling.
Spill append, partial drain, stale file, or invalid journal state can silently lose, duplicate, or partially accept records unless failure paths are explicit and tested.
Overflow spill may leak mmap files or file handles on failure, partial drain, or runner shutdown.
Sustained-overrun tests may be flaky if they depend on timing rather than deterministic capacity/admission control.
Allocation gate may regress if overflow, policy dispatch, or test instrumentation allocates per message on hot paths.

Overflow spill readback: spill file contents are read back during drain and no duplicate or missing entries occur.

acceptance_test_matrix: Sustained overrun semantic coverage for DROP_NEW, DROP_OLD, BLOCK, and OVERFLOW_TO_DISK, asserting admitted, dropped, blocked, spilled, and drained records per edge.

Overflow-to-disk edge-case coverage for spill append, drain ordering, readback correctness, cleanup, stale or invalid spill state, invariant/CRC-equivalent failure, and partial drain or append failure handling.
Hot-swap coverage proving edge-level policy changes affect subsequent writes without corrupting existing in-memory or spilled records.
Configured QA gate coverage requiring qa/smoke.sh, qa/regression.sh, jmhSmokeCheck, and allocation gate to remain green.
assumptions: GraphPartitionRunner owns runtime edge buffering and is the correct boundary for applying per-edge backpressure decisions.
dag-framework-api owns public API types and builder-facing configuration while runtime-core owns execution behavior.
dag-framework-lvc contains reusable MmapJournal machinery that can be used for overflow-to-disk without defining a new spill format.
Existing qa/smoke.sh, qa/regression.sh, and jmhSmokeCheck are the authoritative configured gates for this feature.

acceptance_tests: Sustained overrun matrix covers DROP_NEW, DROP_OLD, BLOCK, and OVERFLOW_TO_DISK.
DROP_NEW rejects new records while preserving already-buffered records under overrun.
DROP_OLD evicts oldest buffered records and admits newer records under overrun.
BLOCK applies bounded blocking without data loss or cross-partition propagation.
OVERFLOW_TO_DISK writes overflow records to an mmap spill file and drains them back correctly.
Edge-level policy hot-swap changes behavior for subsequent edge writes without corrupting buffered or spilled data.
Failure and partial-acceptance cases are covered for spill append/drain errors or interrupted drain paths.
Stale or invalid spill state is rejected or recovered according to existing journal invariants.
MmapJournal invariant failure or CRC-equivalent validation failure is surfaced without silent data loss.
jmhSmokeCheck, qa/smoke.sh, and qa/regression.sh pass.
design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Policy lookup and hot-swap must be thread-safe at edge granularity; BLOCK must block only the overrun edge producer path; DROP_NEW and DROP_OLD must make deterministic single-edge shedding decisions; OVERFLOW_TO_DISK must serialize spill append/drain ordering so in-memory and spilled entries are observed exactly once in edge order.
forbidden_alternatives: A bespoke spill file encoder or non-MmapJournal overflow format.
Global runtime backpressure propagation across partitions.
Priority queues, priority-based drop rules, or custom policy callbacks.
Test-only behavior switches that bypass the production policy implementation.
hard_constraints: Do not add custom backpressure policies or public extension hooks.
Do not add priority-based shedding.
Do not add cross-partition backpressure propagation.
Reuse MmapJournal machinery from lvc-standard for spill persistence.
Allocation gate and jmhSmokeCheck must remain green.
qa/smoke.sh and qa/regression.sh must pass.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: dag-framework-api defines stable public enum and builder configuration surface; runtime-core implements edge buffering, overrun behavior, blocking semantics, hot-swap state handling, and policy dispatch; dag-framework-lvc provides the mmap journal primitive reused for overflow spill persistence; QA roots contain only tests and fixtures.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: OVERFLOW_TO_DISK must reuse MmapJournal machinery from dag-framework-lvc/lvc-standard for spill files, must drain spilled records back through the edge reader, and must clean up or close spill resources after drain without inventing a new spill file format.

acceptance_test_matrix: DROP_NEW sustained-overrun semantic coverage: new records are rejected/dropped while existing queued records remain ordered and drainable.
DROP_OLD sustained-overrun semantic coverage: oldest queued records are evicted, newer records are admitted, and queue capacity invariants hold.
BLOCK sustained-overrun semantic coverage: producer admission blocks until capacity is available and does not propagate cross-partition backpressure.
OVERFLOW_TO_DISK sustained-overrun semantic coverage: records spill through MmapJournal, drain in deterministic order, and readback assertions verify persisted payloads.
Edge-level hot-swap coverage: changing one edge policy at runtime affects only that edge and preserves in-flight queue/spill invariants.
Lifecycle edge-case coverage: stale/invalid spill files, invariant or CRC-equivalent failure, and failure/partial acceptance cleanup are tested.
Configured QA gate coverage: qa/smoke.sh, qa/regression.sh, jmhSmokeCheck, and allocation gate remain green.
assumptions: GraphPartitionRunner owns runtime edge queues and is the correct boundary for policy enforcement and hot-swap.
BackpressurePolicy is a public API concept and should live in dag-framework-api rather than runtime-core internals.
Existing MmapJournal machinery in dag-framework-lvc/lvc-standard can be reused for spill persistence without creating a new on-disk format.
Default behavior should preserve existing runtime semantics unless a policy is explicitly configured.
Allocation gate and jmhSmokeCheck are existing CI/QA gates that must remain green.

acceptance_tests: DROP_NEW under sustained overrun drops newly admitted records while preserving existing queued records.
DROP_OLD under sustained overrun evicts oldest queued records and admits newer records.
BLOCK under sustained overrun blocks admission until capacity is available without cross-partition propagation.
OVERFLOW_TO_DISK under sustained overrun spills records via MmapJournal and drains them back in order.
Overflow spill file readback is asserted during drain and resources are cleaned up.
Edge-level hot-swap changes behavior for only the targeted edge.
Stale/invalid spill state and invariant failure paths fail safely without silent data corruption.
Failure or partial-acceptance paths do not leave queue, spill, or runner lifecycle invariants broken.
design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Policy reads on the hot path must be edge-local and thread-safe, with hot-swap applied atomically per edge; BLOCK may block only the producing path for the configured edge and must not propagate cross-partition backpressure; DROP_NEW and DROP_OLD must maintain queue invariants under concurrent producers/consumers; OVERFLOW_TO_DISK must serialize spill/drain access so FIFO/readback semantics are deterministic.
forbidden_alternatives: A single global policy that cannot be overridden per edge.
A best-effort overflow format unrelated to MmapJournal.
Priority-aware dropping or custom callback policy injection.
Blocking all partitions or upstream graph execution for one overrun edge.
Hot-swap implemented by rebuilding the graph runner.
hard_constraints: Do not add custom backpressure policies.
Do not add priority-based shedding.
Do not add cross-partition backpressure propagation.
Reuse MmapJournal machinery from lvc-standard instead of inventing a new spill format.
Allocation gate must stay green.
jmhSmokeCheck must remain green.
qa/smoke.sh and qa/regression.sh must pass.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: dag-framework-api owns public enum and builder/config surface; runtime-core owns queue admission, drop/block behavior, hot-swap state, metrics/observability if already present, and sustained-overrun semantics; dag-framework-lvc owns mmap journal reuse for spill persistence; QA owns only tests and fixtures.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: OVERFLOW_TO_DISK must reuse MmapJournal machinery from lvc-standard for spill files, preserve record ordering, drain spilled records back before or alongside in-memory backlog according to the documented edge semantics, validate stale/invalid spill state and invariant failure paths, and close/delete temporary spill resources on normal drain and failure cleanup.
design_contract.public_api: Add public enum BackpressurePolicy with DROP_NEW, DROP_OLD, BLOCK, and OVERFLOW_TO_DISK; extend GraphPartitionRunner.Builder with default and per-edge policy configuration keyed by edge/source-target identity; expose edge-level policy hot-swap through a runtime-scoped method or handle without introducing custom policy callbacks.

acceptance_test_matrix: DROP_NEW sustained overrun: newest arrivals are rejected while previously queued entries remain ordered and drain correctly.
DROP_OLD sustained overrun: oldest queued entries are evicted, newer accepted entries drain correctly, and capacity invariants hold.
BLOCK sustained overrun: producer admission blocks or waits without data loss, resumes after drain, and does not propagate across partitions.
OVERFLOW_TO_DISK sustained overrun: excess entries spill through MmapJournal and drain in the expected order.
Overflow spill readback: spill file contents are read back during drain and no duplicate or missing entries occur.
Edge-level hot-swap: changing one edge policy affects only that edge and takes effect for subsequent enqueue decisions.
R-002/snapshot prerequisite coverage: design and review evidence confirm required prerequisite behavior exists before R-006 source changes are accepted.

Lifecycle failure coverage: stale or invalid spill files, invariant or CRC-equivalent failure, spill append failure, partial drain failure, and cleanup paths fail closed without partial acceptance or broken lifecycle invariants.

assumptions: GraphPartitionRunner owns runtime edge queues and is the correct boundary for policy enforcement and hot-swap.
BackpressurePolicy is a fixed public API enum, not a custom extension point or callback mechanism.
dag-framework-api owns public policy symbols and builder-facing configuration while runtime-core owns runtime edge behavior.
dag-framework-lvc contains reusable MmapJournal machinery from the lvc-standard path and must be reused for overflow spill persistence.

R-006 is dependency-gated on the R-002/snapshot prerequisite; the design slice must confirm the prerequisite is present before implementation begins, and missing prerequisite evidence requires repair/replan before source changes.
Policy hot-swap is edge-scoped, visible to concurrent producers and consumers, and must not propagate backpressure across partitions.
Existing qa/smoke.sh, qa/regression.sh, jmhSmokeCheck, and allocation gates are authoritative verification gates for this feature.

acceptance_tests: DROP_NEW sustained overrun rejects newest arrivals while previously queued entries remain ordered and drain correctly.
DROP_OLD sustained overrun evicts oldest queued entries, admits newer entries, and preserves capacity invariants.
BLOCK sustained overrun blocks producer admission until capacity is available, does not lose data, and does not propagate cross-partition backpressure.
OVERFLOW_TO_DISK sustained overrun spills excess entries through MmapJournal and drains them in deterministic order.
Overflow spill readback verifies persisted payloads and proves no duplicate or missing entries across in-memory and mmap-backed boundaries.
Edge-level hot-swap changes behavior only for the configured edge and applies to subsequent enqueue decisions without corrupting existing buffered or spilled records.
Stale or invalid spill files are rejected or recovered according to existing journal invariants.
Invariant or CRC-equivalent MmapJournal validation failures fail closed without silent data corruption or partial acceptance.
Spill append, drain interruption, and partial failure paths leave queue, spill, and runner lifecycle invariants intact.
qa/smoke.sh, qa/regression.sh, jmhSmokeCheck, and allocation gates pass.
design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Each edge reads its current BackpressurePolicy atomically at enqueue time. Hot-swap updates must be thread-safe and edge-local. BLOCK may block only the producing path for the configured overrun edge. DROP_NEW and DROP_OLD must preserve deterministic queue capacity and ordering invariants under concurrent producers and consumers. OVERFLOW_TO_DISK must serialize spill append and drain so in-memory and spilled entries are observed exactly once in documented edge order.
forbidden_alternatives: Stringly typed policy selectors.
User-supplied policy callbacks.
Priority queues or priority-aware drop rules.
Global runtime backpressure state shared across partitions.
Blocking all partitions or upstream graph execution for one overrun edge.
A new spill encoder or non-MmapJournal overflow format.
Test-only behavior switches that bypass production policy implementation.
hard_constraints: Do not add custom backpressure policies or public extension hooks.
Do not add priority-based shedding or conflation.
Do not add cross-partition backpressure propagation.
Do not rebuild the graph runner to implement policy hot-swap.
Do not invent a bespoke spill file format outside MmapJournal.
Confirm R-002/snapshot prerequisite before implementing source changes; if absent, stop and replan.
Allocation gate must stay green.
jmhSmokeCheck must remain green.
qa/smoke.sh and qa/regression.sh must pass.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: dag-framework-api defines the stable public enum and builder/configuration surface; runtime-core implements edge queue admission, DROP_NEW, DROP_OLD, BLOCK, policy dispatch, hot-swap state, and sustained-overrun behavior; dag-framework-lvc provides MmapJournal primitives reused for overflow spill persistence; QA roots contain only tests and fixtures.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: OVERFLOW_TO_DISK must reuse MmapJournal machinery from dag-framework-lvc/lvc-standard, preserve edge record order across in-memory and spilled entries, read back spilled payloads during drain, clean up or close spill resources after normal drain and failure cleanup, reject stale or invalid spill state, and fail closed on invariant or CRC-equivalent validation failure without duplicate delivery, silent loss, or partial acceptance.

acceptance_test_matrix: DROP_NEW sustained overrun: newest arrivals are rejected while previously queued entries remain ordered and drain correctly.
DROP_OLD sustained overrun: oldest queued entries are evicted, newer accepted entries drain correctly, and capacity invariants hold.
BLOCK sustained overrun: producer admission blocks or waits without data loss, resumes after drain, and does not propagate across partitions.
OVERFLOW_TO_DISK sustained overrun: excess entries spill through MmapJournal and drain in the expected order.
Overflow spill readback: spill file contents are read back during drain and no duplicate or missing entries occur.
Edge-level hot-swap: changing one edge policy affects only that edge and takes effect for subsequent enqueue decisions.
R-002 prerequisite coverage: existing snapshot/journal lifecycle assumptions are detected before implementation and remain compatible after overflow spill integration.

Lifecycle failure coverage: stale or invalid spill files, invariant or CRC-equivalent failure, spill append failure, partial drain failure, and cleanup paths fail closed without partial acceptance or broken lifecycle invariants.
Configured QA gates: qa/smoke.sh, qa/regression.sh, jmhSmokeCheck, and allocation gate remain green.
assumptions: GraphPartitionRunner owns runtime edge queues and is the correct boundary for policy enforcement and hot-swap.
BackpressurePolicy is a fixed public API enum, not a custom extension point or callback mechanism.
dag-framework-api owns public policy symbols and builder-facing configuration while runtime-core owns runtime edge behavior.
dag-framework-lvc contains reusable MmapJournal machinery from the lvc-standard path and must be reused for overflow spill persistence.

R-006 is dependency-gated on the existing R-002 snapshot/journal lifecycle contract; design and implementation must first confirm the prerequisite is present and compatible, then integrate without redefining snapshot semantics.
Policy hot-swap is edge-scoped, visible to concurrent producers and consumers, and must not propagate backpressure across partitions.
Existing qa/smoke.sh, qa/regression.sh, jmhSmokeCheck, and allocation gates are authoritative verification gates for this feature.

acceptance_tests: DROP_NEW sustained overrun rejects newest arrivals while previously queued entries remain ordered and drain correctly.
DROP_OLD sustained overrun evicts oldest queued entries, admits newer entries, and preserves capacity invariants.
BLOCK sustained overrun blocks producer admission until capacity is available, does not lose data, and does not propagate cross-partition backpressure.
OVERFLOW_TO_DISK sustained overrun spills excess entries through MmapJournal and drains them in deterministic order.
Overflow spill readback verifies persisted payloads and proves no duplicate or missing entries across in-memory and mmap-backed boundaries.
Edge-level hot-swap changes behavior only for the configured edge and applies to subsequent enqueue decisions without corrupting existing buffered or spilled records.
Stale or invalid spill files are rejected or recovered according to existing journal invariants.
Invariant or CRC-equivalent MmapJournal validation failures fail closed without silent data corruption or partial acceptance.
Spill append, drain interruption, and partial failure paths leave queue, spill, and runner lifecycle invariants intact.
R-002 snapshot/journal prerequisite compatibility is explicitly checked before implementation and remains intact after R-006 changes.
qa/smoke.sh, qa/regression.sh, jmhSmokeCheck, and allocation gates pass.
design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Each edge reads its current BackpressurePolicy atomically at enqueue time. Hot-swap updates must be thread-safe and edge-local. BLOCK may block only the producing path for the configured overrun edge. DROP_NEW and DROP_OLD must preserve deterministic queue capacity and ordering invariants under concurrent producers and consumers. OVERFLOW_TO_DISK must serialize spill append and drain so in-memory and spilled entries are observed exactly once in documented edge order.
forbidden_alternatives: Stringly typed policy selectors.
User-supplied policy callbacks.
Priority queues or priority-aware drop rules.
Global runtime backpressure state shared across partitions.
Blocking all partitions or upstream graph execution for one overrun edge.
A new spill encoder or non-MmapJournal overflow format.
Snapshot or journal lifecycle reimplementation outside the existing R-002-compatible machinery.
Test-only behavior switches that bypass production policy implementation.
hard_constraints: Do not add custom backpressure policies or public extension hooks.
Do not add priority-based shedding or conflation.
Do not add cross-partition backpressure propagation.
Do not rebuild the graph runner to implement policy hot-swap.
Do not invent a bespoke spill file format outside MmapJournal.
Do not redefine or bypass the R-002 snapshot/journal lifecycle prerequisite.
Allocation gate must stay green.
jmhSmokeCheck must remain green.
qa/smoke.sh and qa/regression.sh must pass.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: dag-framework-api defines the stable public enum and builder/configuration surface; runtime-core implements edge queue admission, DROP_NEW, DROP_OLD, BLOCK, policy dispatch, hot-swap state, and sustained-overrun behavior; dag-framework-lvc provides MmapJournal primitives reused for overflow spill persistence; QA roots contain only tests and fixtures.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: OVERFLOW_TO_DISK must reuse MmapJournal machinery from dag-framework-lvc/lvc-standard, preserve edge record order across in-memory and spilled entries, read back spilled payloads during drain, clean up or close spill resources after normal drain and failure cleanup, reject stale or invalid spill state, fail closed on invariant or CRC-equivalent validation failure without duplicate delivery, silent loss, or partial acceptance, and remain compatible with the existing R-002 snapshot/journal lifecycle contract.
design_contract.public_api: Add public enum BackpressurePolicy with exactly DROP_NEW, DROP_OLD, BLOCK, and OVERFLOW_TO_DISK; expose default and per-edge policy configuration through GraphPartitionRunner.Builder keyed by edge identity; expose edge-level policy hot-swap through a runtime-scoped method or handle without custom policy callbacks.

candidate.problem_statement: Implement the R-006 backpressure policy selector so GraphPartitionRunner.Builder exposes per-edge DROP_NEW, DROP_OLD, BLOCK, and OVERFLOW_TO_DISK behavior under sustained overrun, including mmap-backed overflow spill, deterministic drain/readback, edge-level policy hot-swap, and prerequisite-safe integration with the existing snapshot/journal lifecycle.
risk_register: BackpressurePolicy API placement could leak runtime-only concerns into dag-framework-api or conflict with existing builder compatibility expectations.
R-006 may be implemented before confirming the R-002 snapshot/journal prerequisite, causing incompatible spill lifecycle behavior.
BLOCK behavior may deadlock or stall unrelated edges if enqueue and drain paths share executor or lock ownership incorrectly.
DROP_NEW and DROP_OLD can produce off-by-one capacity behavior under sustained overrun if edge buffer boundaries are unclear.
DROP_OLD could violate ordering or cleanup/release guarantees if eviction races with drain.
Policy hot-swap can race with active producers or drainers and mix semantics for a single accepted record unless policy references are atomic and edge-local.
OVERFLOW_TO_DISK may reorder records between memory and disk if append/drain boundaries are not serialized.
MmapJournal reuse may accidentally bypass existing invariant checks, cleanup lifecycle, or validation failure handling.
Spill append, partial drain, stale file, or invalid journal state can silently lose, duplicate, or partially accept records unless failure paths are explicit and tested.
Overflow spill may leak mmap files or file handles on failure, partial drain, or runner shutdown.
Sustained-overrun tests may be flaky if they depend on timing rather than deterministic capacity/admission control.
Allocation gate may regress if overflow, policy dispatch, or test instrumentation allocates per message on hot paths.
